answer.reason: The verses only list Nahor in genealogies and relations (son, brother, husband, father, grandfather) and name him in passing, saying nothing of his own deeds beyond the summary.
doubts: GEN 24:10 'the city of Nahor' names a place, not the man, so it was left out.
GEN 11:24-25 concern the earlier Nahor, father of Terah, and were not used.
JOS 24:2 says only that the fathers served other gods, which is too slight to stand as a clause.
